Accepted.description:
To the publisher: `id` is done and the document is at `revision` (the new one, or the unchanged one when the
command changed nothing). Comes after the `applied` of the same change.
Accepted.title: Accepted

ActuateEntry.description:
Command `command` on `actuator` during `[start, end)` seconds of simulated time.

`command` is the fraction of the actuator's full command, in [-1, 1] for a motor (sign is direction) and
[0, 1] for a thruster. What full command means physically comes from the part (B-03b, B-03c, X-01b, X-01c).
One badge and source cover the entry. `id` names the entry inside the schedule (unique there): commands
that edit an entry name it by id, never by position, so a reordered or partly accepted batch cannot change
a different entry than the one meant.
ActuateEntry.title: ActuateEntry

Actuator.description:
Something on `instance` that a command drives. A motor drives one joint (`joint`); a thruster has none.

`supply` (B-03d) is the instance the actuator draws from: a motor from a `battery` part, a thruster from a `tank`
part (`PartRole`). `None` means the actuator is not metered (nothing runs out). Several actuators may share one
supply; what it holds is spent by all of them (`kinetra_engine.parts.supply`).
Actuator.title: Actuator

AddAssumption.description:
Add an assumption. It must be `editable`: one that is not could never be changed or removed again, so its
inverse would not apply.
AddAssumption.title: AddAssumption

AddControlEntry.description:
Add a schedule entry (an actuate or a separate entry, X-08). `index` is only where it goes in the list; the entry
is known by its `id`.
AddControlEntry.title: AddControlEntry

AddPartDef.description: Put a part definition into the project (`DesignSpec` carries the definitions it uses).
AddPartDef.title: AddPartDef

AddTerrainProp.description: Place a terrain prop (ramp or step) on the planet's ground. `index` is only where it goes in the list.
AddTerrainProp.title: AddTerrainProp

Applied.description:
Revision `revision` of the document exists: `command` (as applied) from `origin` changed it as `changes`
says, and the verdict is now `verdict`. Sent to every subscriber, the publisher included, in revision order.
Applied.title: Applied

Assumption.description: One assumption of the verdict, as the human-review panel shows it.

key.description: Stable machine key, e.g. 'vehicle_mass'. Verdict sensitivities cite it.
key.title: Key

Assumption.title: Assumption

AxisExpr.description:
A length in metres: `offset + sum(factor * param)`. A snap point coordinate in the part's local frame, or a
dimension of a shape component (`shape.py`). Every `param` is a length parameter of the part.
AxisExpr.title: AxisExpr

BodyPose.description: Position [m] and orientation (unit quaternion `x, y, z, w`) of body `body`, in the world frame.
BodyPose.title: BodyPose

BodyRef.description:
A rigid body of the run and the project instances it consists of (welded instances move as one body). `id` is
the body's stable id (G3): a pose's `body`, a contact's `body` and a body `other` name it. A break names a joint
(`Joint.id` of the project), not a body.
BodyRef.title: BodyRef

BodyTarget.description: What a body touched: another body of the run.
BodyTarget.title: BodyTarget

Box.description: Rectangular block. `size_*` are full extents [m] along the component's local x, y, z.
Box.title: Box

BreakEvent.description:
Joint `joint` released because the load on it went over its break threshold (both in N; plan 4.6, a simplified
model). `reason` is the release's cause, `over_threshold` ("임계 초과"): only this one is a break (X-08).
BreakEvent.title: BreakEvent

BreakThreshold.description: Joint load [N] above which the joint releases. A simplified model, not FEM (plan 4.6).
BreakThreshold.title: BreakThreshold

ClearParameter.description: Unset a parameter of an instance: it takes the part's default again.
ClearParameter.title: ClearParameter

CommandBatch.description:
Edits applied in order as one: all of them or none (`client-adapter.md` C2). Every intermediate state
must be a valid `Project` (see the module docstring).
CommandBatch.title: CommandBatch

ComputeTag.description:
⑦ The settings the run actually used: integrator, `timestep_s` [s] and the solver's settings by name
(`NAME_PATTERN`).
ComputeTag.title: ComputeTag

ConditionMetEvent.description: A success condition of the project became true. This is not a verdict (P4): it says the run satisfied it.
ConditionMetEvent.title: ConditionMetEvent

ContactEvent.description:
`body` touches (`phase` `begin`) or stops touching (`end`) `other`. `force` is the contact force at `begin`,
if known.
ContactEvent.title: ContactEvent

ControlSchedule.description:
The time-axis control program. Entries are kept in the order given; time order is not required. Entry ids
are unique inside the schedule.
ControlSchedule.title: ControlSchedule

CoreBuildTag.description: ⑥ The core build: its commit (the force-applying paths and their order are in it).
CoreBuildTag.title: CoreBuildTag

CpuTag.description: ② CPU: architecture (`x86_64`, `arm64`, ...) and model string.
CpuTag.title: CpuTag

Curve.description: Piecewise-linear `y(x)`: at least two points, `x` strictly increasing, in `x_unit` and `y_unit`.
Curve.title: Curve

CustomBuildEngine.description: Built by us: the compiler and the build flags identify the binary (`build_flags` may be an empty string).
CustomBuildEngine.title: CustomBuildEngine

Cylinder.description: Solid circular cylinder. `radius` and `length` [m]; the axis is the component's local z.
Cylinder.title: Cylinder

FixedDistribution.description: No spread: Monte-Carlo uses the nominal.
FixedDistribution.title: FixedDistribution

ForceN.description: A force in newtons (`unit` is always `N`, so a client never guesses).
ForceN.title: ForceN

Frame.description:
The state of run `run_id` at `tick` (`sim_time_s` seconds): every body's pose, and the events since the
previous frame.
Frame.title: Frame

GroundTarget.description: What a body touched: the ground. It has no id (the ground of the planet is one thing), so an `id` is refused.
GroundTarget.title: GroundTarget

Hello.description:
First message of each side: the protocol number it speaks. The core answers a `hello` it can serve with its
own; with a number it cannot serve it answers `error` and closes.
Hello.title: Hello

ImpulseNs.description: An impulse in newton-seconds (`unit` is always `N*s`).
ImpulseNs.title: ImpulseNs

Incline.description: Slope angle above the ground in radians, strictly between 0 and pi/2.
Incline.title: Incline

Instance.description:
One placed part. Parameters not listed take the `PartDef` default. `material` is optional: a part whose
mass is declared by its own specs needs none; `None` means no material is assigned.
Instance.title: Instance

InstanceParameterBinding.description: Bind an assumption to one instance's parameter (the part default when the instance omits it).
InstanceParameterBinding.title: InstanceParameterBinding

Joint.description:
A connection between two snap points of two different instances. `a` is the parent side by convention.

`axis` (hinge and slider): the line the one free motion is about or along, in the frame of the `a` snap point
(`JointAxis`). `None` is +Z of that frame (`DEFAULT_JOINT_AXIS`). A fixed joint has no motion and so no axis.
`limits` are optional (`None`: unlimited, as a wheel axle) and not allowed on a fixed joint; they bound the joint
coordinate, which is 0 at the saved pose (`JointLimits`).
`break_threshold` is optional (`None`: never breaks).
Joint.title: Joint

JointAxis.description:
The direction a hinge turns about or a slider moves along: a unit vector in the frame of the snap point of
the joint's `a` end (the parent side), the same frame a snap point's `orientation` gives. One badge and source
cover the vector. The sense is right-handed for a hinge (positive angle turns `b` counter-clockwise seen from
the tip of the axis) and positive travel is along the vector for a slider. `-axis` describes the same line of
motion with the sign of the coordinate (and so of its limits and of a motor command) flipped.
JointAxis.title: JointAxis

JointLimits.description:
Travel limits of the joint coordinate: rad for a hinge, m for a slider. `lower < upper`.

The coordinate is 0 at the saved pose, so the saved pose must be inside its own limits: `lower <= 0 <= upper`
(a joint saved outside its travel would start in violation of its own limit). Both ends are inclusive.
JointLimits.title: JointLimits

MaterialPropertyBinding.description: Bind an assumption to one physical property of a material carried by the project.
MaterialPropertyBinding.title: MaterialPropertyBinding

MoveInstance.description: Set the stored world pose of one instance.
MoveInstance.title: MoveInstance

NamedCurve.description: A curve a part defines under a name (`torque_speed` for a motor, `thrust` for a thruster).
NamedCurve.title: NamedCurve

Origin.description:
Which input path sent a command (`client-adapter.md` 3.5): the person's mouse or keyboard, the agent's
accepted proposal, a confirmed voice sentence, an XR hand or controller, the MCP server.
Origin.title: Origin

OsTag.description: ① Operating system: kind (`linux`, `macos`, ...) and kernel release.
OsTag.title: OsTag

ParamDef.description: A named parameter of the part with its default and allowed range, all in `unit`.
ParamDef.title: ParamDef

ParamTerm.description: `factor * <value of parameter param>`. The parameter must be a length.
ParamTerm.title: ParamTerm

ParamValue.description: The value of one of the part's parameters for this instance. Unit and range are the `ParamDef`'s.
ParamValue.title: ParamValue

PartRole.description:
What a part is for, where the simulation needs to know (B-03b). A part without a role is only a body.

The actuator on an instance must fit its part's role (`designspec.py`): a motor actuator drives a `motor` part, a
thruster actuator a `thruster` part. What a role requires of the definition is checked by `PartDef` (the
required curves, specs and parameters), so a part that says `motor` always has the numbers a motor needs and one that says
`spring_damper` has its stiffness and damping (B-03e).
PartRole.title: PartRole

PartSpecBinding.description: Bind an assumption to one named specification of a part carried by the project.
PartSpecBinding.title: PartSpecBinding

Placement.description:
Where a prop stands on the ground: centre `x`, `y` [m] and rotation `yaw` [rad] about +Z (counter-clockwise
seen from above). One badge and source cover the whole placement.
Placement.title: Placement

PlatformTag.description:
The eight run conditions of `engine.md` 5.4 (H1). Two tags are the same tag when all eight are equal
(`==`). `image_digest` is required and `None` means "no image" (not a container): leaving it out is an error, so
a run cannot lose that component by omission.
PlatformTag.title: PlatformTag

Pose.description: World pose of an instance's part frame. One badge and source cover the whole pose.
Pose.title: Pose

ProjectChanges.description:
The sections of the project a change replaced, each as its whole new value. A section that is `None` did not
change. `materials`, `parts`, `instances`, `joints`, `actuators`, `schedule` are the parts of `Project.design`;
`world` and `assumptions` are the project's. A change is at the grain of a section, not of an item: a client
that needs finer grain reads `Applied.command`, but never needs to apply it (D3).
ProjectChanges.title: ProjectChanges

PropTarget.description: What a body touched: a terrain prop, by its id in the project's world.
PropTarget.title: PropTarget

ProtocolError.description:
The connection broke the protocol (not a rejected command): bad JSON, a message that is no known message,
a `publish` before `hello` or `subscribe`, an unknown project, a protocol number the core does not speak. A
fatal error is followed by the core closing the connection.
ProtocolError.title: ProtocolError

Quantity.description: One physical number with its unit, badge and source.
Quantity.title: Quantity

RampProp.description: Rises along local +x. `length` is the horizontal run.

material.description: ID of the Material of the prop's surface; None is the planet's ground.
material.title: Material

RampProp.title: RampProp

Reason.description:
Why a command was rejected: a stable `code`, a readable sentence and what it is about. `ids` are typed
refs (`kind` and `id`) because an id is only unique inside its own collection: a part `wheel` and an instance
`wheel` are different things.
Reason.title: Reason

Ref.description:
`id` of a `kind`. A snap point is `<instance>/<snap point>`, a parameter `<instance>/<parameter>`:
those two ids are only unique inside their owner.
Ref.title: Ref

Rejected.description: To the publisher: `id` changed nothing, for these reasons (never empty: C3).
Rejected.title: Rejected

RelinkInstance.description:
Point an instance at another part definition of the project: the way back for an instance whose definition is
missing (C-06, `docs/architecture/missing-definitions.md`; the other ways are `add_part_def` with the missing id
and `remove_instance`). The part must be one the project carries and must suit the instance (its parameters and
its joints' snap points): else the command is rejected with the validator's sentence and the offending ref.
RelinkInstance.title: RelinkInstance

RemoveActuator.description: Remove an actuator with its schedule entries.
RemoveActuator.title: RemoveActuator

RemoveAssumption.description: Remove the assumption with this key. Refused (`not_editable`) when it is not `editable`.
RemoveAssumption.title: RemoveAssumption

RemoveControlEntry.description: Remove the schedule entry with this id.
RemoveControlEntry.title: RemoveControlEntry

RemoveInstance.description:
Delete an instance with its joints, the actuators on it, on those joints or drawing from it (a battery or tank),
and their schedule entries.
RemoveInstance.title: RemoveInstance

RemoveJoint.description: Release a joint, with the actuators that drive it and their schedule entries.
RemoveJoint.title: RemoveJoint

RemoveMaterialDef.description:
Take a material definition out. Rejected while an instance or a terrain prop uses it, unless `unlink` is set:
then the instances that use it stay without a definition (C-06; see `RemovePartDef`). A terrain prop that uses
it still refuses.
RemoveMaterialDef.title: RemoveMaterialDef

RemovePartDef.description:
Take a part definition out. Rejected while an instance uses it, unless `unlink` is set: then the instances
that use it stay as placeholders without a definition (C-06). `unlink` is what the inverse of an `add_part_def`
that gave placeholders their definition says, so that undo can put the placeholders back; the validator refuses
it from any sender (`missing_definition`: a command never creates a placeholder).
RemovePartDef.title: RemovePartDef

RemoveTerrainProp.description: Remove the prop with this id.
RemoveTerrainProp.title: RemoveTerrainProp

ReplaceControlEntry.description: Replace the schedule entry with the same id (`entry.id`), in place. The new entry may be of the other type.
ReplaceControlEntry.title: ReplaceControlEntry

ReplaceJoint.description:
Replace the joint with the same id, in place: same position, and the actuators and schedule entries on it
stay. Changes its limits, break threshold, kind or ends. Rejected if the new joint no longer suits what is on
it (a motor on a joint that is fixed now, a motor whose instance is no longer at an end).
ReplaceJoint.title: ReplaceJoint

ReplaceMaterialDef.description: Replace the material definition with the same id, in place (instances and terrain props keep using it).
ReplaceMaterialDef.title: ReplaceMaterialDef

ReplacePartDef.description:
Replace the part definition with the same id, in place. Instances keep using it, so the new definition
must still suit every one of them (their parameters, their joints' snap points): else the command is
rejected with the validator's sentence and the offending ref.
ReplacePartDef.title: ReplacePartDef

ReplaceTerrainProp.description: Replace the prop with the same id (`prop.id`), in place: move it, resize it, change its incline, height or surface.
ReplaceTerrainProp.title: ReplaceTerrainProp

Resumed.description:
The core continues a subscription from `after_revision`: the `revision - after_revision` `applied` messages
that follow, in order, bring the client's copy to `revision`.
Resumed.title: Resumed

RunCompleted.description: The planned duration was reached. The trajectory hash and its tag are required.
RunCompleted.title: RunCompleted

RunEnded.description:
The run is over. `last_tick` is the tick of the run's last `frame`: the core always sends a frame at the end
tick before `run_ended`, even when the end falls between two frame intervals, so the final poses and every event
after the previous frame reach the client (`check_run`). `end` says how the run ended and carries the trajectory
evidence.
RunEnded.title: RunEnded

RunFailed.description: The engine could not go on: there is no trajectory to hash, so a `trajectory` is refused.
RunFailed.title: RunFailed

RunStarted.description:
A run begins. `revision` and `definition_hash` name the document the run was compiled from, `bodies` is the
fixed body list in the order of the binary pose block, `platform` the platform tag the trajectory hash at the end
belongs to. `frame_every_ticks` is how many ticks lie between two frames.
RunStarted.title: RunStarted

RunStopped.description: A stop was requested and the run ended at `last_tick`. The trajectory up to there has a hash, with its tag.
RunStopped.title: RunStopped

SelectPlanet.description: Put the project on another planet, by id. The planet's constants are not part of any command.
SelectPlanet.title: SelectPlanet

SeparateEntry.description:
Release separator instance `separator` at `at` seconds of simulated time (X-08, `docs/architecture/separation.md`).

One entry of the same time-axis schedule as `ActuateEntry` (no separate staging list); the `type` tag tells them apart.
`separator` is the id of an instance of a `separator` part (B-15). A separation cannot be undone, so the schedule
holds at most one per separator; that rule (and two at one time) is the compiler's (`separation_twice`,
`separation_conflict`, X-01d), not this model's. One badge and source cover the entry.
SeparateEntry.title: SeparateEntry

SeparationEvent.description:
Separator instance `separator` let go of joint `joint` on purpose (X-08): `reason` is `intended_separation` ("의도한
분리"), never a break. Each side received the declared separation `impulse`, equal and opposite. `entry` is the schedule
entry that asked for it, `null` for a manual request during the run. `tick` is the first tick whose state is apart.
SeparationEvent.title: SeparationEvent

SetAssumption.description:
Replace the assumption with the same `key`, in place. Refused (`not_editable`) when the stored one is not
`editable`, and when the new one would change `editable`.
SetAssumption.title: SetAssumption

SetInstanceMaterial.description: Assign a material of the project to an instance; `None` assigns none.
SetInstanceMaterial.title: SetInstanceMaterial

SetParameter.description:
Set a parameter of an instance (unit and range are the part's). `index` is where a parameter that is not
set yet goes in the instance's list; for one that is set already it must be absent.
SetParameter.title: SetParameter

Shape.description:
The recipe: one or more components. At least one is `add`; ids are unique.

The offsets and factors inside the expressions are plain numbers; like a snap point's pose, the recipe carries
one badge and source for all of them (who drew these dimensions: `declared`, or `cite` with a drawing, ...).
Shape.title: Shape

SnapPoint.description:
A place where this part can attach to another. `kind` and `accepts` are compatibility tags (B-04b matches them).

`position` is in metres in the part's local frame and may follow length parameters; `orientation` is the
local frame of the snap point. Badge and source cover the whole pose.
SnapPoint.title: SnapPoint

SnapRef.description: A snap point of a placed instance.
SnapRef.title: SnapRef

Snapshot.description: The whole document at `revision`, of the document life `epoch`.
Snapshot.title: Snapshot

Source.description:
Where a value comes from.

`ref` is what was cited, declared or run: a document, a datasheet, a run id, or the reason a default was chosen
(for an estimate: the method and its inputs). `locator` is where inside it (table, page, section). `url` is a
link when there is one. `license` (SPDX expression over the repo allowlist, `spdx.py`) and `declared_by` / `declared_at` feed the badge popover
(`ValueBadges`, 인용 and 사용자 선언); `Provenance` allows each only on its own badge.
Source.title: Source

SpecDef.description: A named specification (사양): no-load speed, rated thrust, capacity ... Name and unit are the part's.
SpecDef.title: SpecDef

material.description: ID of the Material of the prop's surface; None is the planet's ground.
material.title: Material

ThreadTag.description: ⑧ Thread counts of the physics step and of the solver.
ThreadTag.title: ThreadTag

TrajectoryEvidence.description:
A trajectory hash and the platform tag it belongs to. A hash without its tag is not evidence (H1), so the two
are one object. Two of these are compared only when their tags are equal (H2).
TrajectoryEvidence.title: TrajectoryEvidence

Unit.description: Closed unit vocabulary (SI, written the way the JSON carries it).
Unit.title: Unit

WasmEngine.description: Distributed as a WASM package: the hash of the distributed file identifies the binary.
WasmEngine.title: WasmEngine

WheelEngine.description: Distributed as a package wheel (PyPI): the hash of the distributed file identifies the binary.
WheelEngine.title: WheelEngine

World.description: `planet` is an ID (same pattern as every other ID); `terrain_props` sit on that planet's flat ground.
World.title: World

WorldPosition.description: A position in metres, world frame.
WorldPosition.title: WorldPosition
